source_name: KOZ SR – Konfederácia odborových zväzov SR (mass redundancy guidance + KZVS archive)
why_relevant: Peak union confederation: explains the statutory redundancy procedure from the workforce side and maintains a document library of higher-level collective agreements, which points to which sectors/employers have live agreements and who signed them.

source_name: MPSVR SR – Zoznam uložených a platných kolektívnych zmlúv vyššieho stupňa
why_relevant: Statutory deposit register: employers must lodge higher-level collective agreements with the ministry, which publishes the list and announces representative agreements in Obchodný vestník and Zbierka zákonov. Definitive test of whether banking/finance ever acquires a sector agreement — currently the contested question in SK banking.

source_name: MPSVR SR – Oznámenie o uzatvorení reprezentatívnej KZVS
why_relevant: The formal extension mechanism: a representative KZVS binds non-signatory employers in the sector. Any move toward binding sector-level terms in banking would surface here first as a ministry notice.

source_name: MPSVR SR – Spolupôsobenie odborovej organizácie a zamestnaneckej rady
why_relevant: Defines which employee body (odborová organizácia / zamestnanecká rada / zamestnanecký dôverník) must be consulted in a given bank, and therefore which counterparty to monitor for leaked or published redundancy consultations.

source_name: Slov-Lex – Zbierka zákonov SR (e-Zbierka)
why_relevant: Official consolidated law collection. Act 483/2001 on banks and its amendments (e.g. 30/2026 Z. z., which changed fit-and-proper requirements for key function holders and the appointment/remuneration of the internal control head) directly reshape bank governance roles and leadership appointments — the legal driver behind many 'organization change' events.

source_name: NR SR – parliamentary bill documents (dôvodová správa)
why_relevant: Explanatory memoranda and impact assessments attached to banking bills state intended organisational and staffing consequences months before the law is published — earliest legal-side warning of governance/structure change.

source_name: NBS – makro komentáre on hromadné prepúšťania and unemployment
why_relevant: Central bank analytical commentaries interpret the labour-office redundancy notification series, giving dated, quantified context and occasionally sector breakdowns that the raw ÚPSVaR releases omit.

source_name: Eurofound European Restructuring Monitor – Slovakia restructuring events
why_relevant: EU-level structured database of large restructuring events (job losses/creations, type, sector) with per-case factsheets; ~716 SK cases recorded. Gives a comparable, machine-readable EN-language record of bank/finance restructuring that can be joined to SK-language redundancy notices.

source_name: FinStat – likvidácie / podania z Obchodného vestníka per company
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator that re-indexes Obchodný vestník filings and registry data per legal entity, including union base organisations (e.g. Základná organizácia OZ PPaP at Slovenská sporiteľňa) — a fast lookup layer and a way to enumerate in-bank union legal entities and their status.

source_name: EU-OSHA OSHwiki – Worker participation in Slovakia
why_relevant: English-language structural overview of SK employee representation (odborová organizácia, zamestnanecká rada, zamestnanecký dôverník) and consultation duties — useful bridge document for mapping the workforce-side actors before local-language collection.

source_name: SITA / V Financiách – union-vs-banks bargaining coverage
why_relevant: National wire service with a dedicated finance vertical; carries union statements, mediator requests and SBA rebuttals with dates — the practical trigger feed for the union/legal channel when union sites lag.

source_name: STVR spravodajstvo – public broadcaster coverage of bank labour disputes and redundancies
why_relevant: Public broadcaster reports both union claims and employer/association responses, and separately covers regional mass-redundancy notifications — a corroboration layer for events first visible in labour-office data.

source_name: FinReport.sk – bank headcount and branch-network tracking
why_relevant: Specialist SK finance outlet that compiles per-bank employee and branch counts over time (e.g. Slovenská sporiteľňa, VÚB, Tatra banka headcount/branch deltas since 2018) — the quantitative counterpart to redundancy notices, and often the only public per-employer figure when labour-office data is anonymised.

source_name: SARIO – Shared Service & Business Process Outsourcing Centres sector page
why_relevant: State investment agency's sector overview of the SSC/BPO industry (60+ centres, 40k+ employees), including regional distribution and named investors. Pointer to individual captive/GBS operators including banking back-office and finance shared services outside Bratislava.

source_name: SARIO – news / press releases (investičné projekty, tlačové správy)
why_relevant: SARIO announces closed investment projects with headcount targets and location (e.g. 33 projects, ~3,300 planned jobs). This is the primary channel where nearshore centre expansions in Košice/Žilina/Nitra/Prešov are first disclosed.

source_name: Ministerstvo hospodárstva SR (MHSR) – tlačové správy o investičnej pomoci
source_subtype: ministry press release / state aid decision
why_relevant: Government approvals of investment aid (investičná pomoc) for technology centres and business service centres name the investor, the city and the committed number of new jobs — the legally binding version of a nearshore hiring announcement. Example found: aid approved for Arcondis Solutions in Košice.

source_name: MHSR – Koncepcia podpory centier podnikových služieb na Slovensku (policy paper)
why_relevant: Government strategy document on the business-services sector: baseline headcount, regional distribution, skills pipeline and policy levers. Useful for structural context and for the official Slovak terminology used in later announcements.

source_name: AmCham Slovakia – Business Service Center Forum (BSCF)
why_relevant: Industry association of ~39 member business-service centres (~40,000 experts) incl. banking/financial captives. Member list is a ready-made actor map; annual BSCF conference agendas and speaker lists reveal leadership moves and expansion plans.

source_name: PwC Slovakia – Shared Service Centres practice and SARIO/PwC SSC sector reports
why_relevant: Advisory firm that co-authors the SARIO SSC sector study; provides headcount, function-mix (finance, risk, IT) and city-level splits for business service centres, including financial-services captives.

source_name: Košice IT Valley cluster – news and member directory
why_relevant: Cluster of ~86 members (IT firms, TUKE/UPJŠ, city and self-governing region) credited with ~6,000 new IT jobs in the Košice region; members include delivery centres serving banking clients. News feed carries expansion, graduate-programme and university-industry announcements.

source_name: Mesto Košice – oficiálne stránky: ekonomika / informácie pre investorov / novinky
why_relevant: City publishes investor information and ceremonial-opening announcements for new service centres with headcount figures (e.g. a Holcim business-services branch opening in Košice with ~60 IT specialists and 300–500 planned positions). Same channel is used for financial-sector back-office arrivals.

source_name: Korzár SME – regional daily for Košice and eastern Slovakia
why_relevant: The dominant regional newsroom for Košice/Prešov; covers openings, expansions and layoffs at local delivery centres far earlier and in more detail than national financial press.

source_name: The Slovak Spectator – business section (English-language SK press)
why_relevant: English-language Slovak outlet that consistently reports foreign-parent expansions into Slovak cities, incl. banking (e.g. an HSBC Košice expansion piece). Useful bridge for reporting that foreign HQ press releases do not carry.

source_name: SITA agentúra – economic newswire
why_relevant: Newswire carrying SARIO and ministry investment announcements verbatim, including regional job-creation figures; often the fastest published version.

source_name: Deutsche Telekom IT Solutions Slovakia – career / open positions (Košice)
why_relevant: Largest nearshore IT delivery employer in Košice; observed to be staffing a newly established Competence Center for Credit Risk and Fraud (Košice/Bonn) — a direct signal of financial-risk and fraud/payments work being relocated to eastern Slovakia. Vacancy composition is a leading indicator of function shifts.

source_name: Profesia.sk – employer-scoped job listings by city (e.g. Košice)
why_relevant: Dominant Slovak job board; employer-ID and city-scoped URLs allow per-centre, per-city vacancy counts over time for banking/payments captives (e.g. Deutsche Telekom IT Solutions company_id=31332, DT Services Europe company_id=27037). Best quantitative proxy for nearshore hiring volume outside Bratislava.

source_name: ÚPSVaR – regional labour statistics, vacancies and mass-layoff reporting
why_relevant: Official district-level (okres) unemployment, reported vacancies and mandatory notification of collective redundancies (hromadné prepúšťanie). Confirms or contradicts announced headcount plans in Košice/Žilina/BB/Nitra/Prešov, and open-data files allow time series.

source_name: Technická univerzita v Košiciach (TUKE) – Ekonomická fakulta (Finance, Banking and Investment)
why_relevant: Regional talent pipeline for banking back-office and risk roles; faculty news, career-day and partnership announcements reveal which banks/centres are recruiting graduates in eastern Slovakia. TUKE is also a Košice IT Valley member, linking academia to captive employers.
